# rbtree-lab: project rules
## Commands
- Build & unit tests: ‘make test‘
- Sanitizers: ‘make asan‘ Valgrind: ‘make memcheck‘
- A change is DONE only when all three pass. Always run them; show output.
- Route all allocations in src/rbtree.c through two rb_malloc and rb_free found in src/rb_alloc.c.
## Hard constraints
- NEVER modify include/rbtree.h. It is the graded contract.
- Use include/rbtree.h as a strict reference for allocations and ownership such; every function must follow the rules outlined there.
- Check every allocation. malloc can return NULL; a NULL return must
leave the tree unchanged and return the documented error code.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass. If a test
looks wrong, stop and explain why instead.
- 'rb_insert' must 'rb_malloc + memcpy' its own copy 'k'; it must never store 'key' itself or free it
## Style
- C23. -Wall -Wextra -Werror must stay clean. No VLAs.
- Error handling: goto-cleanup pattern for multi-allocation functions.
- Prefer the smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.
- Every non-obvious loop gets a one-line invariant comment.
## Workflow
- For any multi-file or algorithmic change: propose a plan and wait for
approval before editing.
- Never commit to the git repository.
- [rb_validate must check root-black](feedback_rb_validate_root_black.md) — required invariant even though header comment omits it

# Explain rb_delete fixup — no code changes

This was a read/explain request, not an implementation request. Nothing to edit. Summary below is the answer; exiting plan mode to deliver it and confirm no further action is wanted.

## What's actually in the code right now

- [include/rbtree.h](include/rbtree.h) contract for `rb_delete` (line 19): removes the key, frees the key copy and value, returns 0 or -1 if absent. It says nothing about fixup directly — that's implied by the fact that `rb_validate` (line 27) must keep passing.
- [src/rbtree.c](src/rbtree.c) `rb_delete` (lines 232-277) currently does the BST-only splice (via `rb_splice` and `rb_inorder_successor`) and then **has only a TODO comment at line 267** — the actual delete-fixup loop is not implemented yet. So today, deleting a black node with a non-trivial sibling structure will fail `rb_validate`'s black-height check.
- Insert fixup (lines 160-202) *is* implemented and gives the pattern the delete fixup will follow: a `problemNode` walked up the tree, an if/else split on which side of the grandparent we're on, each branch explicitly written out with a `// (mirror image, swap left/right)` comment rather than a shared helper.

## Standard CLRS delete-fixup, case by case

Setup: after the BST splice, let `x` be the node that now occupies the spliced-in position (possibly `t->nil`) and that carries an "extra black" — this only happens when the node physically removed (or moved) was black. The loop runs `while (x != t->root && x->color == RB_BLACK)`, always assuming **x is a left child** for the cases below.

**Case 1 — sibling `w` is red.**
`w = x->parent->right`. Recolor `w` black, `x->parent` red, rotate left on `x->parent`, then reassign `w = x->parent->right`. This doesn't resolve anything by itself — it converts the situation into one of cases 2-4 with a new (black) sibling, so the loop continues.

**Case 2 — sibling `w` is black, both of `w`'s children are black.**
Recolor `w` red (removing one black from `w`'s side to balance the one missing from `x`'s side), then move the extra-black problem up: `x = x->parent`. Loop condition re-checked from there.

**Case 3 — sibling `w` is black, `w`'s near child (left, since `w` is a right child) is red, far child (right) is black.**
Recolor `w`'s left child black, `w` red, rotate right on `w`, then reassign `w = x->parent->right`. This reshapes into case 4.

**Case 4 — sibling `w` is black, `w`'s far child (right) is red.**
Recolor `w` to `x->parent`'s color, `x->parent` black, `w`'s right child black, rotate left on `x->parent`, then set `x = t->root` to terminate the loop. This is the case that actually restores balance without help from a further iteration.

After the loop, `x->color = RB_BLACK` unconditionally (mirrors insert's `t->root->color = RB_BLACK` cleanup).

**Sibling case:** every one of the 4 cases above has a mirror image for when `x` is a **right** child (`w = x->parent->left`, rotations swapped left/right, "near"/"far" children swapped). Per this project's existing style in insert fixup (lines 181-201), that mirror is written out explicitly as its own `else` branch, not shared via a helper — same convention should carry into delete fixup.

## Note per project memory
[[feedback_rb_validate_root_black.md]] flags that `rb_validate` must check root-is-black even though the header doesn't spell it out — already true in the current `rb_validate` (line 330), and delete fixup must preserve that (case 4's final `x = t->root` step plus the trailing unconditional black recolor is what keeps it true).

## Standard delete-fixup, case by case

Setup: after the BST splice, `x` is the node now sitting in the spliced position (possibly `t->nil`), carrying an "extra black" — this only arises when the physically-removed node was black. Loop: `while (x != t->root && x->color == RB_BLACK)`. Cases below assume **x is a left child**.

Recolor `w` black, `x->parent` red, rotate left on `x->parent`, reassign `w = x->parent->right`. Doesn't fix anything alone — it converts the situation into case 2/3/4 with a new black sibling, and the loop continues.

**Case 2 — sibling `w` black, both of `w`'s children black.**
Recolor `w` red (pulls one black off `w`'s side to balance what's missing on `x`'s side), then push the problem up: `x = x->parent`. Loop re-checks from there.

**Case 3 — sibling `w` black, near child (left) red, far child (right) black.**
Recolor `w`'s left child black, `w` red, rotate right on `w`, reassign `w = x->parent->right`. Reshapes into case 4.

All three pass clean: `make test`, `make asan`, and `make memcheck` — no errors, no leaks. The `rb_delete` fixup and the splice fix are in and verified.
